text.arabic_uthmani: عَسَىٰ رَبُّنَآ أَن يُبْدِلَنَا خَيْرًۭا مِّنْهَآ إِنَّآ إِلَىٰ رَبِّنَا رَٰغِبُونَ

words.gloss_range: hopeful expectation governing a subjunctive replacement clause; locally human petition rather than divine guarantee or loose maybe
words.root_gloss_range: fixed modal hope, expectation, and near-certainty in some divine-speaker contexts; this human speech selects humble hoped-for possibility
words.prose: {{ar:عَسَىٰ}} ({{tr:ʿasā}}) opens the ayah by moving the speakers from self-indicting lament into a governed petition. It is verb-like enough to take a named subject and a subjunctive content clause, yet modal enough to keep the replacement hoped for rather than reported. Because the speakers are human, the word carries humble expectation before their Lord, not the stronger divine-promise force found in other settings. Its placement also sets up the ayah's two-beat logic: hoped future replacement first, emphatic present orientation second. The hope also sits in a restoration field where Lordship, substitution, and betterment cluster in other settings (66:8, 17:8, 18:40), while the open long vowel gives this petition a slower launch before the denser agency and replacement words arrive.

topics.headline: modal verb governs subject and complement
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the opening hope is syntactically organized around divine agency and a governed replacement clause, not left as a free-floating wish.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence identify {{ar:عَسَىٰ}} ({{tr:ʿasā}}) as an uninflected hope verb whose subject is word 2 and whose complement is the following subjunctive clause.

topics.headline: human hope rather than divine certainty
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the speakers asking with humbled expectation after confession, not claiming compensation as already guaranteed.
topics.reason: The broader usage can include stronger divine-promise force, but the local speakers are humans petitioning, so the surviving payoff is humble hopeful expectation.

topics.headline: hope opens the first beat
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah's architecture: a hoped future act is followed by a separate emphatic declaration of present orientation.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence limits the scope of {{ar:عَسَىٰ}} ({{tr:ʿasā}}) to the replacement clause, while the following emphatic clause begins a new assertion.

topics.headline: hope routed through Lord and betterment formulas
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the local hope belongs to a wider Quranic restoration field in which hope, Lordship, substitution, and betterment cluster, while the local grammar still controls the immediate sense.
topics.reason: The cited pairings with Lordship, betterment, and substitution support a formulaic restoration background, but they do not override the local human petition frame.

topics.headline: long opening sound slows the petition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the recitationally open launch of the petition before the denser words of agency and replacement arrive.
topics.reason: The written and audible long final vowel in {{ar:عَسَىٰ}} ({{tr:ʿasā}}) gives the petition an extended onset.

words.gloss_range: our Lord as nominative subject and hoped agent of replacement, with relational and sustaining force attached to the speakers
words.root_gloss_range: lordship, mastery, ownership, sustaining care, nurture, regulation, and bringing to completion; locally the title marks divine agency in hoped provision
words.prose: {{ar:رَبُّنَا}} ({{tr:rabbunā}}) immediately names the agent of the hoped action. Its nominative role keeps the Lord as subject, while the attached plural suffix makes the petition relational: the same group who lost the garden asks as a shared community before their own sustaining Lord. The root field of lordship and nurture makes the requested replacement feel like governed restoration rather than a neutral transaction, and the local provision network ties that Lordship to betterment and substitution rather than mere possession. Because the same title returns later as a destination phrase, this first occurrence begins the ayah's frame: the Lord is first hoped from as provider and later turned toward as goal. The doubled center and fused suffix make the title sound compact and weighty at the start of the request.

topics.headline: nominative Lord-title names hoped agent
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the hoped replacement is not agentless; the Lord is grammatically positioned as the one expected to act.
topics.reason: Local grammar makes {{ar:رَبُّنَا}} ({{tr:rabbunā}}) the nominative subject of the hope construction.

topics.headline: plural possession folds the speakers into the title
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the speakers do not name an abstract deity but their shared Lord, with the petitioning group fused into the title.
topics.reason: The possessive suffix on {{ar:رَبُّنَا}} ({{tr:rabbunā}}) is structurally bound to the title and refers to the same collective speakers.

topics.headline: lordship makes replacement governed care
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the replacement is imagined under sustaining governance and staged care, not as a random swap after loss.
topics.reason: The root range supports master, sustainer, nourisher, and one who brings to completion, while local grammar selects the title as subject-agent rather than a full dictionary list.

topics.headline: Lordship joins betterment and replacement fields
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a wider provision pattern around Lordship, betterment, and substitution, while the local request remains this garden-loss petition.
topics.reason: The co-occurrence rows support a restoration and provision background, but local evidence keeps the claim tied to the ayah's replacement request.

topics.headline: first Lord-title begins the ayah frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the repeated Lord-title framing the ayah: first as hoped source of provision, later as destination of desire.
topics.reason: The same title recurs at word 9 with changed case and role, making the first occurrence the opening side of a local frame.

topics.headline: geminated center gives the title weight
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the compressed sound and fused suffix that make the Lord-title acoustically and relationally weighty at the start of the request.
topics.reason: The doubled middle consonant and attached suffix make {{ar:رَبُّنَا}} ({{tr:rabbunā}}) compact rather than analytically separated.

words.gloss_range: subjunctive complementizer that turns the following replacement verb into the governed content of hope
words.prose: {{ar:أَنْ}} ({{tr:ʾan}}) is the hinge that keeps the first beat from becoming a direct report. It subordinates the following verb to the opening hope and makes the desired replacement both verbal and argument-like: an action hoped for, not an event asserted as already happening. Its lean particle form leaves the surrounding words to carry speaker, agent, and beneficiary marking while it carries the syntactic work of subordination, and its final nasal links audibly into the following beneficiary-marked verb so the complementizer and hoped action cohere as one unit.

topics.headline: particle subordinates the replacement action
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the replacement remains the governed content of hope rather than an independent report of what has happened.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence identifies {{ar:أَنْ}} ({{tr:ʾan}}) as introducing the subjunctive complement clause governed by the opening hope verb.

topics.headline: bare particle marks a tight boundary
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a precise particle boundary between the named subject and the hoped action, keeping the clause verbal and future-facing.
topics.reason: The particle is bare and complementizing, not an emphatic nominal-clause opener; it therefore keeps the following verb in subordinated action form.

topics.headline: nasal sound binds particle to verb
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the complementizer and hoped action cohere as one compact audible unit rather than two coordinated assertions.
topics.reason: The particle supplies subordination, and its final nasal sound links directly into the following beneficiary-marked verb.

words.gloss_range: may He provide us a replacement in exchange; a hoped Form IV act with divine agent, collective beneficiaries, and qualitative object
words.root_gloss_range: replacement, substitution, exchange, alternation, and change across several derived forms; locally Form IV selects giving a substitute to beneficiaries rather than mere alteration
words.prose: {{ar:يُبْدِلَنَا}} ({{tr:yubdilanā}}) carries the action core of the petition. Its hidden singular subject points back to the Lord, while the attached plural object makes the speakers direct beneficiaries of the hoped replacement. The subjunctive mood keeps the act requested rather than narrated. Lexically, the Form IV surface asks for provision of a substitute, not repair of the old garden, while the variant pressure around a stronger form highlights the nearby possibility of intensified transformation without replacing the local Form IV force.

topics.headline: hidden divine subject and attached beneficiaries
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the morphology separating divine agent from human beneficiaries inside one compact verb.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence routes the 3ms subject to the Lord named earlier and identifies the attached plural suffix as object or beneficiary.

topics.headline: subjunctive verb keeps replacement hoped for
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the central action is the requested event of the first beat, not a factual report that replacement has already occurred.
topics.reason: The verb is imperfect subjunctive under {{ar:أَنْ}} ({{tr:ʾan}}), preserving petition and expectation.

topics.headline: Form IV asks for substitute provision
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the request accepts the lost garden as displaced and asks for a new better substitute rather than restoration of the same object.
topics.reason: The root supports replacement and exchange, while the local Form IV frame with beneficiary suffix and explicit object selects giving a substitute.

topics.headline: substitution joins qualitative betterment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the substitution is qualitative: the phrase seeks a better replacement, not merely an exchange of one possession for another.
topics.reason: The local verb, object, and comparison phrase form a replacement-betterment cluster, with cross-reference rows supporting but not controlling that local frame.

topics.headline: variant highlights provision versus transformation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the semantic pressure between providing a replacement and intensively transforming, while the aligned surface keeps provision as the local reading.
topics.reason: The variant rows are useful for contrast, but the local aligned surface is Form IV, so the variant does not govern the canonical parse.

words.gloss_range: an unspecified better good or beneficial replacement, functioning as the exchanged thing and carrying comparative force through the following phrase
words.root_gloss_range: goodness, benefit, wealth, choice, and comparative betterment; locally the object asks for beneficial betterment rather than a named replacement
words.prose: {{ar:خَيْرًا}} ({{tr:khayran}}) supplies the content of the requested substitution. Its accusative indefiniteness leaves the replacement unnamed, but not vague: it is requested as beneficial betterment. The word can be heard as the second object of the substitution and also as qualitative specification, so the request asks for the thing supplied and the quality of the exchange at once. Because the next phrase supplies the comparison base, the broader goodness, benefit, and selection field is locally narrowed into a better good measured against the lost garden. In the wider local network, that good is sought under Lordly provision and in a better-substitution field, so value is foregrounded before the old garden returns as the standard to surpass.

topics.headline: indefinite object names the requested substitute
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the request has a concrete object slot while leaving the actual replacement open to divine provision.
topics.reason: {{ar:خَيْرًا}} ({{tr:khayran}}) is accusative and attached as the explicit object supplied in exchange by the preceding verb.

topics.headline: same form specifies betterment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the word names not only a replacement but the quality the exchange must have: it must be better good.
topics.reason: The accusative form supports object and specification readings within the same substitution frame.

topics.headline: benefit and comparative betterment stay layered
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that material benefit, moral good, and comparative betterment are layered by context instead of being reduced to a thin adjective.
topics.reason: The root range includes goodness, benefit, wealth, and choice, but the following comparison phrase narrows the local use toward beneficial betterment.

topics.headline: goodness joins Lordship and substitution
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the requested good sits in a wider field of divine betterment after loss, while the local phrase still controls the comparison.
topics.reason: The co-occurrence rows link betterment with hope, Lordship, and substitution, but locally the word functions inside this specific replacement request.

topics.headline: value is heard before the comparison base
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that betterment is foregrounded before the lost garden is recalled as the standard to surpass.
topics.reason: The object arrives before the comparison phrase, completing the requested content and then letting the standard follow.

words.gloss_range: comparative phrase meaning than it, with the feminine suffix referring back to the destroyed garden and the preposition retaining separation or source undertone
words.prose: {{ar:مِنْهَا}} ({{tr:minhā}}) closes the petition by naming the standard the better good must surpass. The feminine suffix points back to the known destroyed garden, preventing the comparison from widening into an unnamed worldly reference. At the same time, the preposition does more than mark comparison; it still carries a separation undertone, so the hoped replacement is better than the old garden and no longer bound to it. Whether heard with the better-good object or with the exchange event, the compact phrase stays inside the substitution frame. Placed after the better-good object, the word lets hope lead while the lost possession trails as the comparison base before the ayah turns to assertion.

topics.headline: feminine suffix points to the lost garden
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the comparison is measured against the concrete destroyed garden, not against an abstract or unstated referent.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence resolves the feminine singular suffix in {{ar:مِنْهَا}} ({{tr:minhā}}) to the garden already prominent in the narrative.

topics.headline: comparative min retains departure undertone
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the hoped replacement both surpasses and departs from the old possession.
topics.reason: The local construction requires the comparative function after the better-good word, while the preposition's source or separation range remains a valid pressure.

topics.headline: phrase stays inside the substitution frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the compact phrase belongs to the replacement request whether it is heard as modifying the better object or the exchange event.
topics.reason: Both allowed attachments keep {{ar:مِنْهَا}} ({{tr:minhā}}) within the same local substitution-comparison frame.

topics.headline: comparison closes petition before assertion
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the old garden is recalled last in the petition, just before the speech turns to the speakers' present orientation.
topics.reason: The word follows the better-good object and immediately precedes the new emphatic clause, making it a local hinge.

words.gloss_range: emphatic assertion with first-person plural subject, opening a new nominal clause of present collective orientation
words.prose: {{ar:إِنَّا}} ({{tr:ʾinnā}}) pivots the speech from hoped future replacement into emphatic present self-description. The particle and plural pronoun are fused, so assertion and collective identity arrive together. This second clause does not guarantee the requested substitute; it strongly states the ground of the request: the speakers now define themselves by orientation toward their Lord. Across the boundary with 68:31, the repeated emphatic frame reverses the predicate, carrying the same speakers from confessed excess into declared desire. The long vowel also carries the collective assertion into the following direction phrase, making the audible movement match the declared turn.

topics.headline: assertion and collective self are fused
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the speakers place their collective self inside a strong assertion before the orientation phrase unfolds.
topics.reason: The attached plural pronoun is the governed subject of the emphatic particle.

topics.headline: new clause grounds the hope
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the verse's logic: the substitute is hoped for, but the speakers' present turning is asserted.
topics.reason: {{ar:إِنَّا}} ({{tr:ʾinnā}}) opens a new nominal clause whose predicate comes at the final word.

topics.headline: the declaration performs the turn it states
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the speakers' direct speech enacts their reorientation rather than merely explaining a request.
topics.reason: The emphatic nominal clause describes a durable state and does so as the speakers' own quoted declaration.

topics.headline: same emphatic frame reverses predicate after 68:31
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the same speakers pass from emphatic confession of excess in 68:31 to emphatic declaration of desire in 68:32.
topics.reason: The boundary evidence supports a structural contrast with 68:31, while local grammar keeps this word as the opener of the second clause.

topics.headline: long vowel carries into the direction phrase
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the audible move from vulnerable hope into firm collective assertion and then into direction toward the Lord.
topics.reason: The emphatic particle follows the soft hope modal and its final long vowel opens toward the following direction phrase.

words.gloss_range: directional preposition toward, fronted with the Lord phrase to select positive desire and define the final predicate's orientation
words.prose: {{ar:إِلَى}} ({{tr:ʾilā}}) is load-bearing for the final predicate. It governs the Lord phrase and gives the desire root its positive direction: desire toward and beseeching, not aversion away. Its fronted phrase makes destination the architecture of the declaration before the predicate is named. The word therefore turns desire into a path, routing the speakers away from appetite for the lost garden and toward their Lord. Its long final vowel audibly stretches that direction into the Lord phrase.

topics.headline: preposition selects desire toward
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the preposition decides the predicate's moral and semantic direction: toward the Lord, not away from something.
topics.reason: The desire root is preposition-sensitive, and {{ar:إِلَى}} ({{tr:ʾilā}}) selects the positive toward reading.

topics.headline: fronted destination shapes the declaration
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the destination before the predicate, so the final clause is architected by orientation rather than generic desire.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence places the prepositional phrase with the final predicate, and word order foregrounds it before that predicate appears.

topics.headline: spatial endpoint becomes desire-direction
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices desire being expressed as directed movement toward an endpoint, not as interior appetite alone.
topics.reason: The preposition's endpoint function remains active inside the abstract predicate of desire.

topics.headline: long vowel audibly extends direction
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the sound of direction stretching into the Lord phrase at the center of the final declaration.
topics.reason: The long final vowel in {{ar:إِلَى}} ({{tr:ʾilā}}) suits and reinforces its directional function.

words.gloss_range: our Lord as genitive destination of the fronted direction phrase, completing the final predicate and closing the Lord-title frame
words.root_gloss_range: lordship, mastery, ownership, sustaining care, nurture, regulation, and bringing to completion; locally the title becomes the endpoint of collective desire
words.prose: {{ar:رَبِّنَا}} ({{tr:rabbinā}}) is the same Lord-title, but now in a different role. Governed by the direction word, it becomes the destination that completes the final participial predicate. The plural suffix keeps the speakers' shared relation intact, while the genitive case shifts the title from hoped agent to desired goal. This second occurrence closes the ayah's Lordship frame: the Lord who was asked to provide is the Lord toward whom desire turns. The title's care and authority therefore shape the endpoint, not just the source, of the speech. Its doubled center repeats the compressed sound of the opening title, and this endpoint also participates in a sparse desire-to-Lord formula (94:8) and same-surah reward movement toward being with the Lord in 68:34.

topics.headline: Lord-title governed as destination
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the Lord-title is no longer the subject of hoped action but the governed endpoint of desire.
topics.reason: Local grammar makes {{ar:رَبِّنَا}} ({{tr:rabbinā}}) genitive under the direction preposition and part of the final predicate.

topics.headline: plural relation survives role shift
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the same collective speakers remain bound to the Lord even as the syntax moves them into a destination phrase.
topics.reason: The possessive suffix repeats the collective relation and links the destination phrase back to the speakers.

topics.headline: sustaining Lordship becomes endpoint
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that desire ends not at a neutral destination but at a Lord whose title carries authority, care, and sustaining governance.
topics.reason: The root field gives the endpoint authority and care, while local grammar keeps the selected role as destination under the preposition.

topics.headline: case shift maps provider to goal
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah's structural arc: the same Lord is first the hoped source of replacement and finally the goal of orientation.
topics.reason: The nominative-to-genitive shift between the two Lord-title occurrences creates a local role shift while preserving lexical identity.

topics.headline: sparse formula and surah thread converge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that this endpoint participates in a sparse desire-to-Lord formula and a broader same-surah Lordship thread, including the forward reward location in 68:34.
topics.reason: The supplied recurrence and forward-bridge rows support a formulaic and same-surah background, while the local phrase remains the governing evidence.

topics.headline: geminated title echoes the opening title
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the repeated compressed title sound gathering the plural speakers toward one shared endpoint.
topics.reason: The singular construct title with plural suffix and doubled middle consonant repeats the opening title's acoustic weight at closure.

words.gloss_range: those who are desirous or turning eagerly toward the Lord; an active-participle predicate whose positive valence depends on the preceding direction phrase
words.root_gloss_range: desire, inclination, beseeching, turning toward, and in other prepositional frames aversion or turning away; locally the toward-preposition selects eager orientation
words.prose: {{ar:رَاغِبُونَ}} ({{tr:rāghibūna}}) is the final predicate, so the ayah lands on a durable collective orientation rather than another act of asking. The preceding direction phrase is essential: with it, the root means eager turning toward and beseeching, not aversion. The active participle and plural ending make the speakers themselves bear this orientation as a group-wide state. Across the boundary from 68:31, that state reverses the earlier self-description of excess: expansion is no longer overflow beyond limits but desire governed toward the Lord. The uncommon final predicate leaves aspiration textually before the later reward language in 68:34, and its long plural cadence closes the nominal declaration broadly after the dense chain of collective pronouns.

topics.headline: final active participle marks standing state
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the speakers are characterized by a standing orientation, not merely reported as performing one momentary act of desire.
topics.reason: {{ar:رَاغِبُونَ}} ({{tr:rāghibūna}}) is a nominative active participle functioning as the predicate of the emphatic clause.

topics.headline: plural form makes orientation group-wide
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the whole speaking group, not one individual, is grammatically identified by the final orientation.
topics.reason: The masculine plural participle agrees with the collective subject embedded in the emphatic particle.

topics.headline: preceding direction fixes positive desire
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final word cannot be read apart from its preceding direction phrase; the phrase selects desire toward rather than turning away.
topics.reason: The root changes polarity by construction, and the local prepositional complement selects the positive toward sense.

topics.headline: rare root field makes desire directional
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that this root is not generic wanting; it is a directionally governed desire field whose moral route depends on construction.
topics.reason: Distributional and lexical evidence support positive and negative directions for the root, while the local phrase fixes the positive route.

topics.headline: overflow becomes governed aspiration
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the boundary transformation from uncontrolled excess in 68:31 to expansive desire routed toward the Lord in 68:32.
topics.reason: The ampleness image survives as redirected aspiration, but the local preposition prevents it from becoming unbounded overflow.

topics.headline: marked final desire precedes reward language
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the uncommon final predicate leaves the ayah on aspiration before the later garden-reward field in 68:34.
topics.reason: The occurrence evidence marks the root as uncommon, and the supplied forward rows connect this aspiration with the later reward description in 68:34.

topics.headline: final plural cadence closes the ayah
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah closing on a broad plural cadence that completes the nominal declaration.
topics.reason: The final active participle completes the second beat and supplies the long plural ending of the ayah.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The construction yubdilana khayran minha is enclosed by two occurrences of Rabbina.
baseline_models.mechanism: Replacement is not a self-executing exchange. The repeated Rabb assigns the transfer to an owning authority who can place one thing where another stood, while khayr supplies benefit and chosen excellence as the criterion.

activation_trace.role: Lordship, ownership, and authority frame the substitution as an allocation governed by Rabb rather than controlled by the speakers.
One thing standing in another's place supplies the sentence's basic replacement mechanism.
Chosen excellence makes 'better' a normative selection, not merely a larger quantity.

changed_reading.before: The speakers ask for an unspecified possession superior to a prior one.
changed_reading.after: The speakers relinquish the replacement and its criterion to Rabb: what stands next must be authoritatively placed and genuinely choice-worthy.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: Asa at word 1 governs a requested replacement, and the clause ends with desire directed ila Rabbina.
baseline_models.mechanism: The unusual image of milk whose return is hoped for turns possibility into interrupted provision. Nurturing Rabb can repair and complete what has ceased, while desire moves toward the provider rather than fastening on the absent thing.

activation_trace.role: Hoped return of stopped or uncertain milk materializes asa as expectation after a flow has ceased.
Repair, nurture, and stagewise completion make Rabb the restorer of an interrupted provision.
Desire turning toward or away gives ila Rabbina an explicit redirection away from the missing object.

changed_reading.before: Asa is a generic marker of uncertain optimism about compensation.
changed_reading.after: Asa carries the felt shape of a dried channel that may flow again, with hope redirected toward the nurturing source of provision.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: Yubdilana names change outside the speakers, while inna ila Rabbina raghibun names a changed direction within them.
baseline_models.mechanism: The transformation branch of b-d-l and the directional branch of r-gh-b operate together. The request is not only for a different object; its grammar stages an external alteration alongside an internal reorientation, under Rabb's completing care.

activation_trace.role: Alteration of a thing's form lets substitution carry transformation rather than a simple one-for-one swap.
Desire's ability to turn toward or away supplies the speakers' interior change of direction.
Stagewise nurture links changed circumstances to the repair of those who receive them.

changed_reading.before: Only the lost object's replacement is in view.
changed_reading.after: The sentence asks for a double substitution: a transformed provision and speakers whose desire now faces Rabb.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: Khayran and raghibun meet in a request left deliberately unspecified.
baseline_models.mechanism: Khayr as gift and r-gh-b as both capacity and abundant desirable giving shift the comparison from item quality to a widened economy of receiving. The unspecified better can be greater capacity for bounty, not merely a superior object.

activation_trace.role: Beneficence and gift make khayran something given and circulated rather than only evaluated.
Physical breadth or capacity supplies a vessel-like model for enlarged receptivity.
An abundant desirable gift turns that widened capacity into a possible form of the requested better.

changed_reading.before: Better means a higher-value replacement of the same kind.
changed_reading.after: Better may mean a widened capacity to receive and participate in bounty, changing the economy of desire itself.

context_deltas.mechanism: Context repeatedly couples favorable condition with Rabb, including rescue after threatened exposure. This strengthens a reading of khayran as a cared-for condition of flourishing rather than an inventory comparison.

activation_trace.role: Good condition and favor supply a qualitative state that functions as the means of rescue.
Repair and nurture attach that rescued condition to Rabb's completing care.
Beneficial good anchors the contextual state of favor back to khayran in the focus ayah.

structural_cues: The n-a-m cue recurs at 68:2, 68:34, and 68:49 around Rabb language, spanning favor, flourishing, and rescue.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies favorable condition, rescue, and Rabb's nurture. I infer that these set the comparison scale for khayran; the live alternative is still a concrete material replacement accompanied by favor.

changed_reading.before: The comparative is primarily about possessing a superior thing.
changed_reading.after: The comparative can be about entering a superior condition: rescued, repaired, and held within Rabb's care.

context_deltas.mechanism: The context first presents good as withheld, then stages a plan to block a needy entrant, followed by the planners' own deprivation and confession of injustice. Khayran is therefore revised from private superiority into good whose social route is no longer sealed.

activation_trace.role: Holding the hand back from giving supplies the context's explicit anti-circulation mechanism.
Good as beneficence and gift identifies what the withholding mechanism obstructs.
Entry into an interior supplies the spatial threshold the owners intend to close.
Deprivation and failure to obtain the desired thing reverse exclusion back upon the speakers.
Withholding and detaining from a right gives the confession a distributive mechanism.
Khayr as gift anchors the revised social criterion directly in the requested better.

structural_cues: 68:12, 68:24, 68:27, and 68:29 order withholding, barred entry, experienced deprivation, and confession before the focus request.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies withheld gift, blocked entry, deprivation, and admitted withholding of right. I infer that a genuinely better replacement must reverse that circulation pattern; the alternative is that their ethics and the replacement remain separate matters.

changed_reading.before: They hope to recover a better privately held asset.
changed_reading.after: They hope for a form of good made better by being enterable and shareable, not secured through another person's exclusion.

context_deltas.mechanism: The harvest sequence supplies two independent images of milk or rain being cut off, beside cultivation and deliberate cutting. These images lock onto the focus branch of asa as hoped return of stopped milk, turning the request into an interrupted-yield model.

activation_trace.role: Hoped return of stopped milk provides the focus-side image of a provision channel that may reopen.
Milk cut off from an animal makes the intended harvest-cutting also image an arrested yield.
Cessation of milk or rain supplies a second material image of provision abruptly stopping.
Sowing and cultivation locate the interrupted-flow analogy in a productive cycle.
Replacement gives the reopened yield a new form rather than requiring restoration of the identical object.

structural_cues: The sequence moves from an oath to cut the cultivation, through a cut-off result and arrested provision, to the focus hope for replacement.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies cultivation, deliberate cutting, two cut-yield images, and hoped return of milk. I connect them as an interrupted-provision circuit; the live alternative is coincidental overlap among livestock and orchard branch images.

changed_reading.before: The speakers ask for compensation after total loss.
changed_reading.after: They ask for a ruptured provision circuit to be reopened in a new and better form; loss is an interruption that may educate rather than merely terminate.

context_deltas.mechanism: An oath-backed plan, asserted capability, later self-selection, and speech without certainty expose a failed regime of control. The focus request revises khayran into what Rabb chooses and supplies, not what the speakers guarantee, seize, or define for themselves.

activation_trace.role: A binding oath supplies the owners' initial mode of guaranteeing their intended outcome.
Capability that enables action and possession supplies their confidence in execution.
Choosing or seeking the preferred option exposes self-selection as a contested model of good.
A claim made without certainty diagnoses the fragility of self-guaranteed outcomes.
Lordship and ownership transfer causal and evaluative control to Rabb.
Seeking the better option remains active, but now as delegated choice rather than unilateral preference.

structural_cues: The context moves from their oath and capability to loss, then later interrogates claims that people receive whatever they choose.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies oath, capability, self-selection, and uncertain claim. I infer a transfer from human outcome-control to Rabb's choice; the alternative is a narrower admission that only this one plan failed.

changed_reading.before: They ask the same controlling desire to obtain a superior result by a new route.
changed_reading.after: Asa and Rabbina mark surrendered control: even the definition and selection of 'better' no longer belong solely to them.

context_deltas.mechanism: The plural group first coordinates in lowered speech and then turns face-to-face in reciprocal blame. In the focus, the same plurality acquires a common outward vector, ila Rabbina, so the replacement includes repair of collective orientation.

activation_trace.role: Lowered secret speech supplies the group's first, closed mode of coordination.
A group facing one another gives reciprocal blame a spatially inward circuit.
Blame for what merits reproach supplies the affective force circulating within that group.
Desire turning toward Rabb opens the closed group circuit into a shared external direction.

structural_cues: Plural whispering at 68:23, reciprocal blame at 68:30, plural confession at 68:31, and plural desire at 68:32 form successive group postures.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies closed speech, face-to-face blame, and directed desire. I infer that the group itself is being reconstituted by a new common vector; the alternative is that these are merely successive utterances without social repair.

changed_reading.before: The verse records several individuals jointly asking for compensation.
changed_reading.after: The verse records a damaged collective learning a new shared direction; a better future includes a repaired 'we.'

context_deltas.mechanism: A post-focus sequence shows favor catching a threatened person, Rabb choosing him, and making him among the sound. This supplies a concrete pattern in which divine betterment remakes the recipient, activating the focus transformation branch alongside external replacement.

activation_trace.role: Catching up and reaching the endangered person initiates the rescue mechanism.
Favor and good condition function as what catches and preserves the recipient.
Rabb's repair and nurture connect rescue to a process of completion.
Selection and drawing near supply the transition from rescue to chosen status.
Causing something to become a new state supplies explicit recipient-transformation.
Soundness opposed to corruption names the resulting human condition.
Transformation of form anchors the later remaking pattern back to yubdilana.

structural_cues: 68:49-50 orders interception by favor, selection by Rabb, caused change of state, and resulting soundness.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies rescue, favor, selection, caused change, and soundness. I infer that the focus gift can include making its requesters fit recipients; the live grammatical alternative confines yubdilana to replacing what is given to them.

changed_reading.before: Better is wholly external: changed property for unchanged recipients.
changed_reading.after: The requested substitution can carry a second gift, the repair of the recipients into people able to inhabit the better condition.

context_deltas.mechanism: Later context pairs gradual taking with extended time. That weakens any easy equation of delay with nurturant restoration: asa must retain real uncertainty because an apparently open interval can serve opposite trajectories.

activation_trace.role: Taking degree by degree supplies a hidden adverse trajectory unfolding through stages.
Extension of time and respite provide the interval in which that trajectory can remain unread.
Hope for return remains anchored in asa but cannot be promoted from hope to guarantee.

structural_cues: The post-focus sequence at 68:44-45 places gradual movement inside an extended delay whose outcome is not apparent to its subjects.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies adverse gradation and temporal extension. I infer that elapsed time alone cannot certify restorative nurture; the alternative is that this warning addresses a different audience and does not qualify the speakers' hope.

changed_reading.before: The interrupted flow model makes eventual restoration feel strongly implied.
changed_reading.after: Restoration remains live but not promised; asa protects the request from treating delay, growth, or replacement as an entitlement.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This reading activates the non-dominant r-b-w target carried by the split mapping of focus r-b-b, so it is form-distant and must be described as resonance, not as the ordinary lexical sense of Rabb. It remains anchored in the packet's exact focus mapping and coheres with substitution, unripe growth, and cultivation.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The two Rabb occurrences surround a request for transformed betterment, while asa also carries an unripe palm-stage image.

activation_trace.role: Nurture and growing up, from the non-dominant mapped root, recast Rabb-framed replacement as growth through stages.
Palm spadix and unripe dates supply a not-yet-ripe material state capable of becoming better.
Transformation of form lets replacement unfold as maturation rather than instantaneous exchange.
Sowing and cultivation give the growth resonance a context-grounded productive process.

changed_reading.before: Rabb replaces one mature object with another mature object.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, Rabb may replace through cultivation: the better arrives as regrowth and maturation, including maturation of the requesters.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: The burrow image is a remote branch of kh-y-r and should be rendered only as a spatial analogy. It remains valid because it attaches directly to khayran and is activated by the context's enclosed garden and barred entry; it must not be presented as the lexical meaning of 'better.'
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: Khayran at word 5 is the requested alternative to an antecedent enclosure, and desire now points beyond that enclosure toward Rabb.

activation_trace.role: Coaxing an animal from one burrow opening by obstructing another supplies an exit-through-loss mechanism for khayran.
A garden enclosed or concealed by trees provides the spatial interior from which the old ownership pattern must emerge.
Entry into an interior supplies the contested opening that the owners tried to close.
Desire turning toward Rabb names the direction taken after forced emergence from the closed interior.

changed_reading.before: Better is another, improved enclosure to possess.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, the obstruction itself opens another exit: better is release from the enclosed desire that made the former possession destructive.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This cross-domain link between the opening pen image and orchard cutting is surprising and sequence-dependent. It remains anchored in focus b-d-l transformation and exact context cutting branches, but downstream prose should call it a compositional analogy, not an etymological claim.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: Yubdilana can activate alteration of form, leaving room for a replacement produced through corrective reshaping.

activation_trace.role: Cutting and paring a hard object to level it supplies a productive cut that prepares an instrument of inscription.
Cutting and separation supply the destructive harvest-cut against which productive reshaping is contrasted.
Alteration of form anchors the contrast of cuts in a focus request for transformative substitution.
Repair and completion assign the corrective reshaping to nurture rather than mere destruction.

changed_reading.before: The lost cultivation is simply exchanged for another.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, the failed destructive cut is answered by a formative cut: Rabb rewrites the pattern by reshaping both provision and possessors.

strongest_changes: Khayran becomes unwithheld and enterable good after the sequence of exclusion, deprivation, and confession.
Cut-off milk and rain images activate asa's hoped-return image, making the verse a model of interrupted provision rather than generic optimism.
The speakers relinquish control over both outcome and criterion, moving from oath and asserted capability to Rabb's choice.
Plural desire toward Rabb repairs the group's direction after covert coordination and reciprocal blame, while later rescue leaves recipient-transformation live.
summary.what_was_special: The packet produced unusually tight material bridges between stopped yield and hoped return, while also supporting coexisting social, agential, temporal, and recipient-transforming readings rather than one resolved interpretation.
remaining_uncertainties: The lactation convergence may be a powerful material analogy or an accidental meeting of distant branch images.
The recipient-transformation reading exceeds the narrowest grammatical scope of replacing what is supplied, though the focus's changed desire keeps it anchored.
The r-b-w growth activation depends on a non-dominant split mapping and must remain explicitly exploratory.
The later delay warning may qualify the focus hope or may address a distinct audience without weakening it.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Replacement sought from the nurturer, not seized by plan.** `ر ب ب B001/B002` supplies authority and repair, `ب د ل B001` substitution, `خ ي ر B001/B002` good and chosen excellence, and `ر غ ب B001` desire turned toward. The repeated *rabbanā* encloses replacement and desire. I infer confession reorients agency -> hope for a better substitute; the ayah reverses “our field/our capacity” into receptive dependence.
2. **Transformation remains distinct from replacement.** `ب د ل B002` permits alteration of state without a new substance, while `خ ي ر B003` supplies choosing the better option. The comparative *khayran minhā* can point to another garden, but the branch inventory also leaves room for a changed relation to provision. I infer that “better” may concern moral configuration as well as object quality; the ayah preserves replacement and transformation as coexisting readings.
3. **Desire widened after constriction.** `ر غ ب B002/B004` adds capaciousness and abundant desirable gift. This follows their narrowed distribution (`ق د ر B004`) and deprivation. I infer turning toward the Lord reopens a field of desire no longer bounded by the destroyed possession; *rāghibūn* reads as spatial and affective re-expansion.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 68:34 supplies a later image of what “better” may entail: gardens of well-being located with the Lord. 68:38's “whatever you choose” also creates a corrective contrast between desire turned toward the Lord and preference projected into a self-authorizing book.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Hope as waiting for stopped yield to return.** Fixed `عَسَى` activates `ع س ي B006` (a she-camel whose stopped milk is hoped to return). Deprivation in 68:27, requested replacement here, and gardens of ease in 68:34 supply stoppage and possible resumed provision; I infer that repentance reopens hope as one waits for a blocked flow to return. `عَسَى` thus carries agricultural uncertainty rather than easy optimism.
2. **Two nonexclusive kinds of change.** Fixed `يُبْدِلَنَا` activates `ب د ل B001` (one replacement taking another's place) and `ب د ل B002` (transformation of state without replacement). The lost garden and the speakers' changed confession in 68:29-31 supply an external object and altered agents; I infer two coexisting arrows: lost garden → better garden, and former possessors → transformed people. The request need not choose between material substitution and moral alteration.
3. **Desire reoriented toward the giver rather than the asset.** Fixed `خَيْرًا` activates `خ ي ر B003` (choosing the better option), and fixed `رَاغِبُونَ` activates `ر غ ب B004` (abundant desirable gift). The repeated `رَبُّنَا / رَبِّنَا` places source around both change and desire; I infer that their selection criterion has shifted from controlling a particular garden to seeking good from its nurturer. The ayah reads as a change in the direction and object of appetite.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 68:33 prevents hope from becoming easy optimism, while 68:34 supplies the image of restored garden-ease. Those later ayat preserve the uncertainty of fixed `عَسَى` (`ع س ي B006`) and keep both replacement and transformation branches of `يُبْدِلَنَا` active.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_channel: [P2 68:17-33] The Orchard Moves from Assay to Cultivation, Cutting, and Meal
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Productive value is disclosed through a staged cycle: weathering and test, prepared soil, ripened growth, harvest, and consumption.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: The owners are themselves processed like the orchard: wear and testing reveal condition, while planning, cutting, and morning consumption specify the material sequence they try to control.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Soil Is Prepared and Growth Is Tended
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: Seed enters worked ground, cultivation compacts a route through the field, and sheltered vegetation rises toward fruiting.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: tree-covered orchard (`quranic:root_000266:B003/m02`); dense rising vegetation (`quranic:root_000266:B011/m02`); earning through labor (`quranic:root_000303:B001/m01`); casting seed into prepared soil (`quranic:root_000303:B002/m01`); worked or trampled field (`quranic:root_000303:B008/m01`); tending and completion (`quranic:root_000532:B002/m03`); persistent green plant (`quranic:root_000532:B012/m02`); pollinating tall palms (`quranic:root_000946:B014/m01`); palm cluster and dates (`quranic:root_001015:B005/m01`).
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: The orchard is a managed system rather than an undifferentiated abundance. Soil preparation, seed, compacted access, tending, palm pollination, and fruit cluster each occupy a different role in production.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_channel: [P2 68:17-33] Water and Milk Must Keep Moving Through a Managed Circuit
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: A living resource remains productive only when rain, stored water, pasture, herd movement, and milk transfer continue through connected stages.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: The garden’s loss is reframed as a broken hydrological and husbandry circuit: dew, trough, repeated watering, pasture, lactation, and access can each be the point of arrest.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Cessation Appears as Dry Rain, Cut Milk, and Denied Access
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: Rain or milk stops, the final remnant is drawn, an animal or person waits for return, and deprivation names the failed flow.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: rain and milk cut off (`quranic:root_000305:B005/m01`); lactation severed (`quranic:root_000861:B006/m01`); final remnant at cessation (`quranic:root_000861:B007/m01`); waterless isolation (`quranic:root_000861:B010/m01`); hope that milk returns (`quranic:root_001015:B006/m01`); deprivation of provision (`quranic:root_000313:B008/m01`); beneficial wet provision (`quranic:root_000152:B002/m01`); recovery from depletion (`quranic:root_000152:B003/m01`).
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.ayah_anchors: 68:17/20/22 forms of `ص ر م` [ص ر م]; 68:25 `حَرْدٍ` [ح ر د]; 68:27 `مَحْرُومُونَ` [ح ر م]; 68:32 `عَسَىٰ` [ع س ي]; surface anchor unavailable for root `ب ل ل`.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Cessation is not one shortage. It can occur in sky, udder, last draw, isolated terrain, or gatekeeping. The hope in 68:32 is thereby materialized as the uncertain return of a life-sustaining flow.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_channel: [P2 68:17-33] Loss Reorients Desire Toward Replacement and Repair
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: After deprivation, hope becomes a directed search for a substitute that restores function and exceeds the lost provision.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: Replacement is not a reset: it can change only outward form, occupy another’s place, restore a depleted flow, or answer desire with a more generous provision.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Substitution and Repair Restore a Failed Function
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: One thing takes another’s place or changes form; tending and recovery seek to make the replacement function better than what failed.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: substitute occupying another’s place (`quranic:root_000095:B001/m01`); changed form (`quranic:root_000095:B002/m01`); gradual repair (`quranic:root_000532:B002/m04`); recovery after wasting (`quranic:root_000152:B003/m02`); selection of the better option (`quranic:root_000452:B003/m01`); compatibility through association (`quranic:root_000844:B004/m01`).
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.ayah_anchors: 68:17 `أَصْحَٰبَ` [ص ح ب]; 68:19/29/32 forms of `ر ب ب` [ر ب ب]; 68:32 `يُبْدِلَ` [ب د ل] and `خَيْرًا` [خ ي ر]; surface anchor unavailable for root `ب ل ل`.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Replacement has two distinct operations: exchange the occupant, or transform the existing form. Repair and compatibility then test whether the new arrangement truly restores the broken function.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_channel: [P2 68:17-33] Loss Reorients Desire Toward Replacement and Repair
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: After deprivation, hope becomes a directed search for a substitute that restores function and exceeds the lost provision.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: Replacement is not a reset: it can change only outward form, occupy another’s place, restore a depleted flow, or answer desire with a more generous provision.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Directed Desire Seeks a More Generous Provision
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: Desire turns toward a chosen good whose spaciousness and generosity answer the constriction of loss.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: desire directed toward or away (`quranic:root_000575:B001/m01`); spacious capacity (`quranic:root_000575:B002/m01`); abundant desirable gift (`quranic:root_000575:B004/m01`); beneficial good (`quranic:root_000452:B001/m02`); selected excellence (`quranic:root_000452:B002/m02`); generosity (`quranic:root_000452:B005/m02`); hope of returning milk (`quranic:root_001015:B006/m02`); favor and need answered (`quranic:root_000532:B016/m02`).
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.ayah_anchors: 68:32 `خَيْرًا` [خ ي ر]; 68:29/32 forms of `ر ب ب` [ر ب ب]; 68:32 `عَسَىٰ` [ع س ي] and `رَٰغِبُونَ` [ر غ ب].
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Desire is directional and capacious. It leaves the destroyed object, turns toward the giver, and asks not merely for equivalence but for a more spacious, generous, and durable good.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_channel: [P2 68:17-33] Worship Redirects Blame into Redress and Giving
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Corrective speech exonerates the giver, acknowledges wrong, and restores outward movement through worship, acceptance, and generosity.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: Praise is not isolated ritual language; it changes the social direction of goods by replacing exclusion and self-justification with accepted fault, protected relation, and largesse.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Generosity Reopens the Arrested Flow
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: Good deed, recovery, gift, and largesse move provision outward after deprivation has exposed the harm of enclosure.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: excellent benefaction (`quranic:root_000153:B003/m01`); witnessed good deed (`quranic:root_000154:B003/m01`); recovery and welfare (`quranic:root_000152:B003/m03`); generosity (`quranic:root_000452:B005/m03`); abundant gift (`quranic:root_000575:B004/m02`); gracious provision (`quranic:root_000532:B016/m03`); noble character (`quranic:root_000994:B008/m01`); dew-like giving (`quranic:root_001486:B004/m01`); generous hand (`quranic:root_001487:B008/m01`).
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.ayah_anchors: 68:17 `بَلَوْ` [ب ل و]; 68:19/29/32 forms of `ر ب ب` [ر ب ب]; 68:21 `تَنَادَ` [ن د و]; 68:32 `خَيْرًا` [خ ي ر] and `رَٰغِبُونَ` [ر غ ب]; 68:33 `عَذَابُ` [ع ذ ب]; surface anchors unavailable for roots `ب ل ي`, `ب ل ل`, and `ن د ي`.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Generosity is the inverse of the owners’ plan at the level of flow. It converts possession into outward provision, while good deed and recovery show that giving can restore both social relation and material condition.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak sözü, gerçekleşmeye yaklaşmayı umut, beklenti ve kimi bağlamlarda kaygıyla birlikte bildiren bir görev sözünü açıkça gösterir. Tanrı kaynaklı bildirimlerde ise sonucun kesin sayılması ile insanda umut uyandırılması biçimindeki iki açıklama aynı özel kullanım alanında korunmalıdır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Bu dal yalnız görev sözü anlamını kapsar; sertleşme, yaşlanma, kararma ve adlandırma dallarını kapsamaz.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım, genel görev sözü kullanımını Tanrı'nın bildirisine özgü kesinlik veya umut uyandırma kullanımından ayrı tutar.

concept_map.definition: Bir durumun gerçekleşmeye yakın olduğunu, gerçekleşmesinin umulduğunu ve kimi bağlamlarda kaygıyla beklendiğini bildiren görev sözüdür. Tanrı kaynaklı bildirimlerde sonuç kesin sayılabilir veya söz insanda umut uyandırma amacıyla açıklanabilir.

facets.statement: Gerçekleşmeye yaklaşma ile umutlu, bazen de kaygılı beklentiyi bildirir.
Tanrı kaynaklı bildirimde bir açıklama sonucu kesin sayar, başka bir açıklama ise insanda umut uyandırma işlevini öne çıkarır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynakların ortak çekirdeği yaklaşma, umut ve beklentidir; kaygılı bekleyiş de bu çekirdeğe eşlik edebilir. Tanrı kaynaklı kullanım, kesin sonuç ile insanda umut oluşturma açıklamaları arasında sunulur.

concept_gloss.text: yaklaşma, umut ve kaygılı beklenti bildiren; Tanrı bildirince özel kesinlik taşıyabilen görev sözü
concept_gloss.applicability: Genel görev sözü çekirdeği ile Tanrı kaynaklı bildirime özgü açıklamaların birlikte temsil edilmesi gerektiğinde kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Yaklaşma, umut, kaygılı beklenti ve özel bildirimdeki kesinlik ayrımını birlikte korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Bir olayın gerçekleşmesine yönelik umudun öne çıktığı, yakınlık ve kaygının bağlamdan anlaşıldığı cümlelerde uygundur.

error_profile.preserves: Gerçekleşmeye yönelik olumlu beklentiyi doğal Türkçe içinde korur.
error_profile.loses: Yaklaşma derecesini ve kaygılı bekleyiş olasılığını açıkça söylemez.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Gerçekleşmeye yakınlığın umut veya kaygıdan daha belirgin olduğu bağlamlarda kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Olayın gerçekleşmeye yakın oluşunu belirgin biçimde korur.
error_profile.loses: Umut ve kaygılı beklenti bileşenlerini tek başına ifade etmez.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Tanrı kaynaklı bildirimin kesin sonuç olarak yorumlandığı özel açıklama için kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Özel bildirimde sonucun kesin kabul edilmesi yorumunu korur.
error_profile.loses: Sözün insanda umut uyandırdığı yönündeki diğer açıklamayı dışarıda bırakır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak sözü genel olarak bir şeyin kuruyup sertleşmesini, ayrıca çalışmaktan elin kalınlaşmasını ve bitkinin kalınlaşıp kabalaşmasını birlikte verir. Bu özel gerçekleşmeler genel fiziksel değişimin altında tutulduğunda dal çerçevesi kaynakla uyumludur.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal fiziksel kuruma, sertleşme ve kalınlaşmayla sınırlıdır; umut, yaşlılık veya gece karanlığı anlamı taşımaz.

lexicalization_scope.note: Genel kuruyup sertleşme çekirdeği, elin çalışmayla kalınlaşması ve bitkinin kalınlaşması biçimindeki kalıba bağlı özel kullanımlardan ayrılır.

concept_map.definition: Bir şeyin kuruyarak sertleşmesi ve dayanıklılık kazanmasıdır; çalışmaktan elin kalınlaşması ile bitkinin gelişirken kalınlaşıp kabalaşması bu fiziksel değişimin özel gerçekleşmeleridir.

facets.statement: Bir şey kurur, sertleşir ve daha katı bir duruma gelir.
El, sürekli çalışmanın etkisiyle kalınlaşır ve sertleşir.
Bitki büyürken gövdesi veya dokusu kalınlaşıp kabalaşır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar kuruma, sertleşme ve katılaşmayı ortak çekirdek olarak verir; elin işten kalınlaşması ile bitkinin kalınlaşması bu çekirdeğin belirli katılımcılardaki özel görünümleridir.

concept_gloss.text: kuruyup sertleşme; elin işten, bitkinin gelişirken kalınlaşması
concept_gloss.applicability: Genel fiziksel sertleşme çekirdeği ile el ve bitkiye özgü kalınlaşma kullanımlarının birlikte gösterilmesi gerektiğinde uygundur.

error_profile.preserves: Kuruma ve sertleşme çekirdeğiyle el ve bitkideki özel kalınlaşmaları korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Herhangi bir şeyin kuruma sonucunda katı ve sert duruma gelmesini anlatan genel bağlamlarda kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Genel kuruma ve sertleşme sürecini eksiksiz biçimde korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Sürekli çalışmanın elde oluşturduğu kalınlaşma ve sertleşme anlatılırken kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: El katılımcısını, çalışma nedenini ve ortaya çıkan kalınlaşmayı korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Bitkinin dokusunun veya gövdesinin gelişirken kalın ve kaba duruma gelmesini anlatır.

error_profile.preserves: Bitki katılımcısını ve kalınlaşıp kabalaşma sonucunu korur.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Kuruyup sertleşme sürecini ve el ile bitkiye özgü kalınlaşma kullanımlarını içerir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Taş ve verimsiz toprak dahil farklı varlıklardaki genel katılık ve kuruluk durumuna yayılır.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dal da kuruluk ve sertlik durumunu merkezine alır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Bu dal değişimi süreç olarak verir ve el ile bitki kullanımını ayrıca taşır; komşu dal daha geniş varlık alanındaki sertlik ve kuruluğu durum olarak adlandırır.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Kuruma sonucunda sertleşmeyi ve belirli katılımcıların kalınlaşmasını bildirir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Kalınlık, dokunun sıkılığı ve akmayı ya da uzamayı engelleme gibi daha geniş sonuçları kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki dal sertlik ve kalınlık alanında belirgin biçimde örtüşür.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Bu dal kuruma ve sertleşme değişimine dayanır; komşu dal kuruma koşulu olmadan kalınlık, yoğunluk ve engelleme özelliklerini de kapsar.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Kuruyarak sertleşme ile el ve bitkinin kalınlaşmasını anlatır.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Pürüzlülük, kabalık ve sertliği dağ, arazi, insan ve hayvan gibi geniş bir katılımcı kümesine yayar.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Sertlik ve kabalaşma özellikleri iki dalda ortak bir alan oluşturur.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Bu dal fiziksel bir kuruma veya kalınlaşma sürecidir; komşu dal pürüzlülük ve kabalığı da içeren daha geniş bir nitelik kümesidir.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Bütün adaylar değerlendirildi; en yararlı sınırlar genel sertlik ve kuruluk, kalınlık ve yoğunluk, ayrıca pürüzlü kabalık dallarıyla kuruldu.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak sözü özellikle yaşlı erkeğin daha da yaşlanmasını ve ömrünün ilerleyen yönüne geçmesini bildirir. Dalın katılımcısı genel olarak her yaşlanan varlık değil, kaynakta açıkça belirtilen yaşlı erkektir.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Anlam yaşlı erkeğin ileri yaşa varmasıyla sınırlıdır; genel eskilik, nesnelerin yaşlanması veya yalnız yaşlı kişi adı değildir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Yaşlı erkeğin özne olduğu iki söz dizimi, bu yaşlanma sürecini adlandıran biçimden ayrı fakat aynı çekirdeğe bağlı tutulur.

concept_map.definition: Yaşlı bir erkeğin yaşı daha da ilerleyerek ömrünün ileri dönemine varmasıdır.

facets.statement: Yaşlı erkek daha da yaşlanır ve ömrünün ileri dönemine yönelir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynakların ortak anlatımı, yaşlı erkeğin yaşının ilerlemesi ve ömrünün ileri dönemine varmasıdır; farklı biçimler aynı süreç için verilir.

concept_gloss.applicability: Katılımcının yaşlı bir erkek olduğu ve onun ileri yaşa doğru ilerlemesinin anlatıldığı kullanımların tamamında uygundur.

error_profile.preserves: Yaşlı erkek katılımcısını ve yaşının daha da ilerlemesi sürecini korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Öznenin yaşlı bir erkek olduğu açıkça bilinen ve ileri yaşa varmasının anlatıldığı cümlelerde kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Bağlamdaki yaşlı erkek katılımcısını ve ileri yaşa varma sürecini korur.

lexical_glosses.target_gloss: yaşlı erkek daha da yaşlanıp ömrünün ileri dönemine varmak

neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dal yaşlı erkeğin yaşının ilerlemesini ve ömrünün ileri dönemine yönelmesini bildirir.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Verilen kanıt kartlarında katılımcı, süreç ve yaş sınırı aynıdır; bu nedenle anlam sınırları içinde birbirinin yerine geçebilirler.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Yaşlı bir erkeğin daha da yaşlanması sürecine odaklanır.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Yaşlı erkek ve kadını, yaşlılık durumunu ve yaşlanmayı daha geniş biçimde kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dal insanın yaşının ilerlemesini ve yaşlılık durumunu paylaşır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Bu dal yaşlı erkek katılımcısının ileri yaşa varmasıyla sınırlıdır; komşu dal kadınları, kişi adlarını ve genel yaşlılık durumunu da içerir.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Yaşlı erkeğin ömrünün ileri dönemine doğru yaş almasını bildirir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: İnsanların yanında şarap ve kılıç ağzı gibi nesnelerin eskiliğini de yaşlılık adıyla kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki dal insanda ileri yaş ve yaşlanma alanında örtüşür.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Bu dal yalnız yaşlı erkeğin ilerleyen yaş sürecidir; komşu dal yaşlı kişi adını ve nesnelerin eskiliğini de kapsayan daha geniş bir sınıftır.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Bütün adaylar değerlendirildi; tam eşleşen ileri yaş dalı ile katılımcı veya kapsam bakımından daha geniş iki yaşlılık dalı en açıklayıcı karşılaştırmaları sağladı.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak sözü iki biçimde de gecenin özne olduğu kararma olayını bildirir; bir anlatım karanlığın şiddetlenmesini, diğeri gecenin kararmasını söyler. Bu nedenle dal, genel karanlık adı değil gecenin koyulaşma sürecidir.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Anlam yalnız gecenin kararıp karanlığının şiddetlendiği kullanıma bağlıdır; bütün karanlık olaylarına genellenmez.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım yalnız gecenin özne olduğu kalıba bağlıdır ve buradan yalın bir kök anlamı veya genel kararma anlamı çıkarmaz.

concept_map.definition: Gecenin kararması ve karanlığının daha yoğun bir duruma gelmesidir.

facets.statement: Gece kararır ve karanlığının yoğunluğu artar.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar gecenin kararmasında birleşir; biri karanlığın şiddetlenmesini, diğeri gecenin karanlık duruma geçmesini öne çıkarır.

concept_gloss.applicability: Gecenin özne olduğu ve karanlığın ortaya çıkmasıyla birlikte yoğunlaşmasının anlatıldığı kalıba bağlı kullanımlarda uygundur.

error_profile.preserves: Gece katılımcısını, kararma sürecini ve karanlığın yoğunlaşmasını korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Gecenin karanlık duruma geçip karanlığının yoğunlaştığını doğal bir cümlede anlatmak için kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Gece katılımcısını ve karanlığın belirgin biçimde artmasını korur.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Gecenin kendisinin kararması ve karanlığının yoğunlaşmasıyla sınırlıdır.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Geceyi karanlık kılma ve yoğun karanlığı nitelik olarak taşıma kullanımlarını da kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dal gecenin belirgin ve yoğun karanlığını anlatır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Bu dal yalnız gecenin kararma sürecini verir; komşu dal geçişsiz kararmanın yanında karanlık kılmayı ve yoğun karanlık niteliğini de kapsar.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Gecenin karanlıklaşma sürecini ve karanlık yoğunluğundaki artışı bildirir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Geceyi gündüzün karşıtı bir zaman bölümü olarak, süresi ve çeşitli nitelemeleriyle birlikte kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki dal gecenin karanlığı alanında doğrudan kesişir.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Bu dal gecenin kararma olayına bağlıdır; komşu dal gecenin kendisini, zaman değerini ve karanlık niteliklerini kapsayan daha geniş bir alandır.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Gece öznesinin kararmasını ve karanlığının şiddetlenmesini bildirir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Gecenin bir şeyin üzerine çöküp onu siyahlığıyla örtmesi ilişkisini içerir.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dal gecenin gelmesiyle oluşan karanlık durumu paylaşır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Bu dal gecenin kendi durum değişimidir; komşu dal gecenin başka bir şeyi karanlıkla örtmesi biçimindeki katılımcı ilişkisini gerektirir.

identity_judgment.rationale: Bu dal, kanıtta tek üretken kök çekirdeğine indirgenmeyen sınırlı adlandırma malzemesini taşır. Yapısal bölme şartı koşmadan, yalnız verilen biçim ve bağlam sınırı içinde kontrollü adlandırma kümesi olarak tutulmalıdır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Bu kayıt genel kök anlamı gibi genişletilmemeli, içindeki öğeler birbirinin yerine geçen tek bir sözlük karşılığı sayılmamalı ve yalnız kanıtın verdiği adlandırma sınırı içinde kullanılmalıdır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Kapsam verilen biçim, adlandırma veya özel kullanım sınırıyla bağlıdır; ortak bir yalın anlam ya da üretken genel kullanım varsayılmaz.

concept_map.definition: Kanıt, tek bir kavram yerine hurma alanında iki ayrı adı birlikte listeler: hurma salkımının dalı ve ham hurma. Bu iki gönderge yapısal olarak ayrılmadan olağan bir ortak tanım kurulamaz.

facets.statement: Bir ad hurma salkımının dalını gösterir.
Başka bir ad, henüz olgunlaşmamış ham hurmayı gösterir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kanıt, tek bir birleşik anlamdan çok sınırlı veya biçime bağlı adlandırmaları gösterir; dal bu kayıtları kontrollü biçimde görünür tutar.

source_details.summary: Tek tanıklık, hurma salkımının dalı ile ham hurmayı aynı dal altında iki ayrı ad olarak verir.

concept_gloss.text: hurma salkımının dalı ve ham hurma adları
concept_gloss.applicability: Bu karşılık, kanıttaki iki sınırlı hurma adlandırmasını birlikte göstermek gerektiğinde kullanılır; tek ve üretken bir genel kök anlamı değildir.

error_profile.preserves: Hurma salkımının dalı ile ham hurma göndergelerini ve bunların sınırlı adlandırma niteliğini korur.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Dal yalnız sınırlı veya biçime bağlı adlandırma malzemesini tuttuğu için yayımlanacak güvenilir komşu ayrımı seçilmedi.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak sözü iki yakın fakat eş olmayan süt durumunu bir araya getirir. Bir anlatım dişi devenin sütü olup olmadığının belirsizliğini söyler ve geri dönüş umudunu açıkça belirtmez; diğeri sütü kesilmiş develerde sütün geri gelmesinin umulmasını açıkça kurar.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal süt yokluğu veya belirsizliği gösteren deve adlarıyla sınırlıdır; geri dönüş umudu yalnız ikinci kaynak açıklamasının zorunlu parçasıdır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım, devenin süt durumunu adlandıran yalın adlarla sınırlıdır ve bunları genel umut bildiren görev sözü anlamına genişletmez.

concept_map.definition: Sütü kesilmiş ya da sütü olup olmadığı belirsiz dişi deve veya develere verilen addır. Sütü kesilmiş develeri anlatan kullanımda sütün geri dönmesi umulur; belirsizlik kullanımında bu umut açıkça zorunlu değildir.

facets.statement: Ad, sütü bulunmayan veya sütü olup olmadığı belirsiz dişi deve ya da develeri gösterir.
Sütü kesilmiş develeri anlatan açıklama, sütün geri dönmesine yönelik umudu ayrıca belirtir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Ortak alan devenin süt yokluğu veya süt konusundaki belirsizliğidir. Bir açıklama yalnız sütün bulunup bulunmadığının bilinmemesini, diğeri kesilen sütün geri gelmesine yönelik umudu öne çıkarır.

concept_gloss.text: sütü kesilmiş ya da sütü olup olmadığı belirsiz deve; kesilmede geri dönüş umulur
concept_gloss.applicability: Süt durumu belirsiz tek bir dişi deveyi veya sütü kesilip geri gelmesi beklenen deve topluluğunu birlikte kapsayan açıklamada kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Süt belirsizliğini, süt kesilmesini ve yalnız kesilme kullanımındaki geri dönüş umudunu korur.

contextual_glosses.text: sütü olup olmadığı belirsiz dişi deve
contextual_glosses.applicability: Tek bir dişi devenin o sırada sütü bulunup bulunmadığının bilinmediği kullanım için uygundur.

error_profile.preserves: Dişi deve katılımcısını ve süt varlığı konusundaki belirsizliği korur.

contextual_glosses.text: sütü kesilmiş, geri gelmesi beklenen develer
contextual_glosses.applicability: Bir deve topluluğunun sütü kesildiğinde ve sütün yeniden gelmesi beklendiğinde kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Çoğul deve katılımcısını, süt kesilmesini ve geri dönüş beklentisini korur.

neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Sütün kesilmesini meme ucunun kesilmesi, bozulması veya kuruması gibi nedenlerle birlikte adlandırır.

neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Bu dal belirsizlik veya geri dönüş umudunu gerektirebilir; komşu dal gerçek süt kesilmesine ve bunun bedensel nedenlerine odaklanır.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Tek bir dişi devenin belirsiz süt durumunu veya sütü kesilen develerde geri dönüş umudunu adlandırır.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Bir topluluğun bütün develerindeki süt azlığını veya yokluğunu ve böyle geçen yılı kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki dal develerde sütün azalması veya bulunmaması alanını paylaşır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Bu dal belirli deve adlarına ve kimi kullanımda geri dönüş beklentisine bağlıdır; komşu dal sürü veya topluluk düzeyindeki kıtlığı da kapsar.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Sütün yok veya belirsiz olduğu durumu ve kimi kullanımda geri gelme umudunu adlandırır.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: İki sağım arasında sütün gerçekten yeniden memede toplanmasını ve bu aralığı bildirir.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dal kesinti sonrasında sütün yeniden bulunması olasılığıyla ilişkilidir.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Bu dal yokluk veya belirsizlik durumundaki hayvanı adlandırır ve dönüşü yalnız bekler; komşu dal sütün fiilen yeniden toplanması olayını bildirir.

root_profile.summary: Kök; yaklaşma, umut ve kaygılı beklenti bildiren görev sözünden kuruyup sertleşmeye, yaşlı erkeğin ileri yaşına ve gecenin koyulaşmasına uzanan çok anlamlı bir yapı gösterir. Ayrıca hurmayla ilgili iki ayrı adlandırma ile sütü kesilen ya da süt durumu belirsiz develere verilen adlar bulunur; hurma alanındaki iki ad mevcut dalda ayrı adlandırmalar olarak görünür.
